description: Intent i035 (SNAPSHOT=s09, BRANCH=alloc-multiply-overflow) complete. FINDING (medium confidence): drivers/virt/fsl_hypervisor.c ioctl_memcpy() in snapshots/s09, lines 218-240 with consuming loop at 274-287 — the exact seed sizing-chain analogue. Untrusted source: struct fsl_hv_ioctl_memcpy copied via copy_from_user (line 165) with unrestricted u64 param.count; the only guards (218-220) reject count==0 and 64-bit wraparound of the addition. Missing guarantee: 'unsigned int num_pages' (155) is assigned '(param.count + lb_offset + PAGE_SIZE - 1) >> PAGE_SHIFT' (221), truncating the 64-bit sum to 32 bits with no clamp, and 'kmalloc(num_pages * sizeof(struct fh_sg_list) + sizeof(struct fh_sg_list) - 1, GFP_KERNEL)' (239-240) is a plain 32-bit multiply-add (32-byte element) with no kcalloc/array_size/struct_size check; e.g. count near 2^41 gives num_pages ~2^29 whose product 2^34 wraps to 0, so kmalloc(31) succeeds. Unsafe use: 'for (i = 1; i < num_pages; i++)' (274) writes sg_list[i].source/.target/.size into the undersized buffer, and get_user_pages_fast (249-250) plus the fh_partition_memcpy hypercall (290-291) use the same untruncated count. Within-function asymmetry: the sibling 'pages = kcalloc(num_pages, sizeof(struct page *))' (229) is overflow-checked. Candidates classified: fsl_hypervisor 239/274 reported; fsl_hypervisor 229 safe; block/partitions/ldm.c:1247 safe (on-disk vblk_size bounded to <=512 by ldm_get_vblks perbuf=512/size loop at 1352-1376 and num clamped 1..4 at 1232-1235, product <=2048 cannot wrap; rec*size memcpy offset stays in-bounds); usbip seed chain present UNPATCHED (usbip_common.c:473 store, 664-665 'int size = np * sizeof(*iso)' -> kzalloc at 677, loop at 699-703, error returns without reset) and recorded as excluded-by-rule. Limitations: the whole-tree regex sweep was not run before the finalize directive, so allocator-adjacent sites outside fsl_hypervisor/ldm/usbip are unexamined; the reported finding is a source-level hypothesis (no runtime reproducer; needs ~2^27 pinned pages and /dev/fsl-hv access on Freescale powerpc); the ldm safe classification rests on the in-file caller read (only call site found).
